newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products turn narrowly mixed late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products turn narrowly mixed late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products turned narrowly mixed on late Monday, with players forecasting higher prices for Los Angeles jet fuel as arbitrage opportunities opened up on the East Coast.
"The cargo traders are looking to buy up the stuff," one trader said.
Two cargoes of jet -- one at 300,000 barrels and a second at 250,000 -- arrived in Los Angeles last week, causing prices to drop 4.50-cent and leaving excess supply for resale.
After a slow start, jet fuel edged up a cent late to 68/69 cents a gallon.
Traders also said premiums for CARB diesel diverted refinery production away from jet and kept supply relatively tight.
Strength in futures also helped, with NYMEX November heating oil up 2.64 cents a gallon to 67.70 cents. Futures firmed on news of problems at a BP Ohio refinery and further Middle East tensions.
NYMEX November crude also reacted to the bullish news by settling 96 cents higher at $25.62 a barrel.
Bids for low sulphur diesel climbed a half cent to 71.50 cents with offers frozen at 72 cents.

As predicted by traders, Los Angeles conventional regular gasoline stayed relatively stable, down one cent late to 61.50/62.50 cents a gallon. San Francisco grades remained at the normal discount of 1.50 cents.
CARB-grade gasoline was seen stable at 67.50/68.50 cents, with deals heard done at 67.50 cents for October delivery and 69 cents for November.
